findings: OpenColorIO's BT.709 OETF is a C1-continuous moncurve built from gamma 1/0.45 and offset 0.099; BT.709-6 publishes rounded constants (4.5, 0.018), so the two differ by up to 5.3e-5 near the break. A port follows the published piecewise form.

DJI's D-Log white paper publishes encode and decode with independently rounded constants (decode 3.89616, 2.27752); decode(encode(x)) differs from x by up to 4.4e-7. A port reproduces each published equation.
Camera input transforms in OpenColorIO use CAT02 (ARRI, Sony, Canon) or Bradford (Panasonic, RED, Apple) to reach the ACES white; CG7 must record the adaptation per transform.

Camera log files carry the curve's 10-bit code values as Y' with a limited-range tag (S-Log3 grey Y' 420 = '41% IRE'); a decoder that maps limited to full range before the curve misreads it. The 10-bit ramp fixtures follow that convention and say so in the manifest.
The original ten color.* effects differ by one code value between backends at some fractional settings (21 of 273 renders); the plan called them exact.

Vector generator run 2 failed: 'dji-dlog round trip 4.4e-7' against 1e-10. Cause: DJI's rounded decode constants (finding 2). Rerun with a per-curve 1e-6 bound and a recorded note.
